Updated assessment with SLOOS overlay:
- Core message: The FOMC held the target range at 4.25–4.5% and signaled a modestly easier liquidity stance by slowing the Treasury runoff cap to $5B starting in April, while keeping the MBS cap unchanged at $35B. Growth remains solid, unemployment low, inflation somewhat elevated, and uncertainty higher; one dissent favored continuing the faster balance-sheet runoff.
- SLOOS signals: Banks report stronger demand across C&I, CRE, residential real estate, autos, and credit cards, broadly spanning large, middle-market, and small firms. Reported demand is tied to customer investment, inventory, accounts receivable, and M&A. At the same time, banks have raised minimum credit score requirements for consumer loans and expect higher delinquencies and charge-offs.
- Read-through: Stronger loan demand tilts the near-term macro/market tone modestly more positive versus the FSR-only lens, reinforced by slower QT. But tighter underwriting and expected credit deterioration (with ongoing CRE risks) keep the overall stance cautious.

Net: mildly positive, but guarded.
